title: LedgerBridge seeded weaknesses (SIMULATED fixture)
disclaimer: These entries drive the offline mock provider. They are fixtures, not model output. A flaw is only emitted when its applies_when condition matches the current extracted architecture.

security: Segmentation and inspection between the corporate network and the AWS VPC are not described.
On-premises patching and access model for the ledger VMs is not provided.
resilience: Last DR test results and the manual failover runbook for Oracle are not supplied.
Secondary connectivity (second VPN tunnel or Direct Connect) is not described.
finops: VPN / data-transfer volumes and cloud billing data are not supplied.
compliance: Data-processing inventory and the legal basis for the us-east-1 analytics replica are not supplied.
performance: Batch throughput measurements and VPN bandwidth figures are not supplied.
operability: Monitoring integration plan for cloud resources and batch delivery verification are not described.

flaws.title: Reporting database listener is open to the internet
flaws.description: The security group {components} admits 0.0.0.0/0 on TCP 1521 (Oracle listener). The reporting replica holds personal settlement data and is meant to be reached only through the VPN.
flaws.scenario: Internet attacker -> reaches the Oracle listener -> exploits listener vulnerabilities or guesses credentials -> reads personal settlement data.
flaws.impact: Direct exposure of regulated financial data to the internet; bypasses the corporate perimeter.
flaws.recommendation: Restrict 1521 to the VPN CIDR / reporting subnets, place the database in private subnets only and remove the public route.
flaws.validation_method: Review effective security group rules and run an external port scan.
flaws.reasoning: tool SEC-NET-001 parsed the CloudFormation security group ingress.

rebuttal.argument: The SecurityGroupIngress entry explicitly allows CidrIp 0.0.0.0/0 on port 1521.

flaws.title: Partner exchange bucket is publicly readable
flaws.description: {components} uses AccessControl: PublicRead. Settlement files exchanged with the partner may be exposed to anyone who can guess or list object names.
flaws.scenario: Third party enumerates the bucket -> downloads settlement instruction files containing account data.
flaws.impact: Disclosure of financial transaction data and possible fraud enablement.
flaws.recommendation: Make the bucket private and share files with the partner via pre-signed URLs, bucket policy for the partner's role, or SFTP.
flaws.validation_method: Check bucket ACL and public access block; use S3 Access Analyzer.
flaws.reasoning: tool SEC-STO-001 found a PublicRead ACL.

rebuttal.argument: The ACL is declared PublicRead in the template.

flaws.title: Partner gateway function role allows all actions on all resources
flaws.description: The Lambda execution role {components} carries an inline policy with Action "*" and Resource "*". The internet-facing partner gateway can therefore administer the whole AWS account if compromised.
flaws.scenario: Malicious partner payload exploits the gateway code -> function role credentials used to read archives, change IAM and delete queues.
flaws.impact: Account-wide compromise from a partner-facing integration.
flaws.recommendation: Scope permissions to the settlement queue, the archive bucket prefix and CloudWatch logs only.
flaws.validation_method: IAM Access Analyzer policy generation from CloudTrail.
flaws.reasoning: tool SEC-IAM-001.

rebuttal.argument: The inline policy statement is Allow * on * as recorded by the IAM check.

flaws.title: Partner API key is embedded in the function environment
flaws.description: {components} defines the partner API key as a literal environment variable in the template (value redacted). It will be visible in CloudFormation, the Lambda console and any code repository holding the template.
flaws.scenario: Anyone with read access to the stack or repository obtains the partner credential and can submit instructions as LedgerBridge.
flaws.impact: Credential exposure for a system that submits financial instructions.
flaws.recommendation: Store the key in Secrets Manager or SSM SecureString, resolve it at runtime and rotate the exposed key.
flaws.validation_method: Search history for the literal; confirm rotation with the partner.
flaws.reasoning: tool SEC-SEC-001.

rebuttal.argument: A literal secret-like value is present in Environment.Variables.

flaws.title: Trust boundary between corporate network and AWS relies on a single VPN with no described segmentation
flaws.description: The VPN is the only path between the data centre and AWS, and the material does not describe route filtering, network segmentation or traffic inspection across it. A compromise on either side may have unrestricted reach into the other.
flaws.scenario: Compromised corporate workstation reaches reporting and partner gateway subnets over the VPN.
flaws.impact: Lateral movement across the hybrid boundary.
flaws.recommendation: Define routed segments, restrict VPN routes to required prefixes and inspect traffic at the boundary.
flaws.validation_method: Review route tables, firewall policy and VPN configuration.
flaws.reasoning: document states the VPN is the only path; no segmentation described.

rebuttal.argument: No segmentation design is part of the supplied material.
rebuttal.concede_argument: The described segmentation and filtering covers the boundary concern; withdrawing.

flaws.moderator_note: The mainframe SNA gateway named in the claim is not part of this architecture; claim is unsupported.
flaws.title: Mainframe SNA gateway exposes unauthenticated LU6.2 sessions
flaws.description: The mainframe SNA gateway accepts unauthenticated LU6.2 sessions from the corporate network.
flaws.scenario: Internal attacker opens an LU6.2 session and injects ledger transactions.
flaws.impact: Unauthorised transaction injection.
flaws.recommendation: Require session authentication on the gateway.
flaws.validation_method: Gateway configuration review.
flaws.reasoning: SEEDED HALLUCINATION - refers to a mainframe gateway that does not exist in this architecture.

rebuttal.concede_argument: No mainframe or SNA gateway is part of this architecture; the claim was wrong.
rebuttal.argument: No such gateway exists.

flaws.title: Personal data is replicated outside the EU (possible control gap)
flaws.description: A reporting replica is placed in us-east-1 for the global risk team while the requirements state EU data residency for account-holder data. Relative to GDPR Art.44-46 and the organisational residency policy this is a possible control gap; a lawful transfer mechanism may exist but is not documented.
flaws.scenario: Personal settlement data is stored and accessed outside the EU without a documented transfer basis.
flaws.impact: Potential residency/transfer non-conformance and audit finding.
flaws.recommendation: Document the transfer mechanism and data minimisation (pseudonymised aggregates) or keep the replica in an EU region.
flaws.validation_method: Confirm replica region, fields replicated and DPO-approved transfer basis.
flaws.reasoning: deployment regions include us-east-1 while residency requirement states EU.

rebuttal.argument: A replica in us-east-1 conflicts with the stated EU residency requirement unless a transfer basis is documented.
rebuttal.concede_argument: The described pseudonymisation / transfer basis addresses the residency concern; withdrawing.

flaws.title: Reporting database holding personal records is not encrypted at rest (possible control gap)
flaws.description: {components} is declared without storage encryption while tagged as personal customer records. Relative to GDPR Art.32 and ISO 27001 A.8.24 this is a possible control gap.
flaws.scenario: Snapshot copy or storage access outside normal controls exposes personal settlement data.
flaws.impact: Weaker confidentiality of personal data at rest.
flaws.recommendation: Enable encryption with a customer-managed KMS key for the instance and its replicas.
flaws.validation_method: Check StorageEncrypted and key policy.
flaws.reasoning: tool SEC-ENC-001.

rebuttal.argument: StorageEncrypted is false for the personal-data instance.

flaws.title: Ten-year retention is not technically enforced on the archive (possible control gap)
flaws.description: {components} holds settlement records subject to a 10-year retention period but declares no lifecycle, object lock or retention configuration. Retention and later deletion therefore rely on manual action. Relative to GDPR Art.5(1)(e) this is a possible control gap.
flaws.scenario: Records are deleted early by mistake or retained beyond the allowed period without evidence.
flaws.impact: Cannot demonstrate retention and deletion controls during audit.
flaws.recommendation: Configure object lock (compliance/governance mode) and lifecycle rules matching the retention schedule.
flaws.validation_method: Review bucket retention configuration against the schedule.
flaws.reasoning: tool COMP-DATA-001 plus the stated retention requirement.

rebuttal.argument: No retention mechanism is declared on the archive bucket.

flaws.title: Auditable access to the archive is not demonstrated (possible control gap)
flaws.description: The requirements state archive access must be auditable but the template defines no CloudTrail data-event logging or access logs. Audit logging may exist at account level.
flaws.scenario: Auditor requests who accessed settlement records; no evidence can be produced.
flaws.impact: Gap in accountability for access to personal financial data.
flaws.recommendation: Enable CloudTrail data events and S3 access logging for the archive with protected, retained storage.
flaws.principle: ISO 27001 A.8.15; ACME-SEC-006 Logging and detection
flaws.validation_method: Review CloudTrail configuration and log retention.
flaws.reasoning: tool COMP-LOG-001 found no audit-trail resources.

rebuttal.argument: No audit logging resource is part of the supplied infrastructure.
rebuttal.concede_argument: An organisation trail with data events covers the requirement; withdrawing.

flaws.title: Settlement delivery depends on a single VPN path with no secondary circuit
flaws.description: All traffic between the data centre and AWS crosses one site-to-site VPN. The 2025-11-06 incident shows that a tunnel drop causes the nightly batch to miss the partner cut-off; no secondary tunnel, second customer gateway or Direct Connect is described.
flaws.scenario: Tunnel or gateway failure at 02:00 -> settlement files cannot reach the partner gateway -> cut-off at 05:30 missed.
flaws.impact: Missed settlement windows and partner SLA breaches; already experienced once.
flaws.recommendation: Add redundant tunnels/gateways (and ideally a diverse Direct Connect path), automate failover and alert on tunnel state.
flaws.validation_method: Fail the primary tunnel in a test window and measure batch delivery.
flaws.reasoning: one VPN connection resource; incident report documents the outage.

rebuttal.argument: A single VPN connection is declared and the incident report confirms the impact.

flaws.title: Ledger database standby shares the primary data centre and failover is manual and untested
flaws.description: The Oracle standby is in the same data centre as the primary and failover is manual, last tested two years ago. A site-level event would exceed the 4-hour RTO, and the 1-hour RPO cannot be evidenced.
flaws.scenario: Data-centre power or network loss -> both primary and standby unavailable -> recovery depends on restoring from backups of unknown currency.
flaws.impact: RTO/RPO objectives for the system of record are not credibly met.
flaws.recommendation: Establish an off-site standby or cloud DR copy, automate failover and run a documented DR test at least annually.
flaws.validation_method: DR exercise with timed recovery and measured data loss.
flaws.reasoning: document states same-site standby and stale DR test; no off-site copy described.

rebuttal.argument: The document itself states the standby is in the same data centre and the failover test is two years old.

flaws.title: Settlement queue has no dead-letter queue
flaws.description: {components} defines no redrive policy. A poison settlement file would be retried until retention expiry, blocking processing and risking loss of a settlement instruction.
flaws.scenario: Malformed settlement file -> repeated failures -> backlog -> missed cut-off with no isolation of the bad message.
flaws.impact: Silent loss or blocking of settlement instructions.
flaws.recommendation: Add a DLQ with redrive policy and alarm, and make the gateway idempotent.
flaws.validation_method: Inject a malformed message in test and verify DLQ routing.
flaws.reasoning: tool RES-MSG-001.

rebuttal.argument: No RedrivePolicy is present on the settlement queue.

flaws.title: Reporting database is single-AZ with minimal backups
flaws.description: {components} sets MultiAZ: false with a one-day backup retention. Regulatory reporting becomes unavailable on instance or AZ failure and recovery depends on a single daily backup.
flaws.scenario: AZ failure during month-end reporting -> reports unavailable until restore.
flaws.impact: Reporting outages around regulatory deadlines.
flaws.recommendation: Enable Multi-AZ and extend backup retention to match reporting criticality.
flaws.validation_method: Confirm MultiAZ and backup retention; test restore.
flaws.reasoning: tool RES-HA-001.

rebuttal.argument: The reporting database is not on the settlement critical path and reports can be regenerated, so the business impact is lower than for the ledger; the single-AZ configuration is still a confirmed weakness.

flaws.title: Bulk settlement and replication traffic over the VPN has unquantified transfer cost
flaws.description: Nightly settlement files, GoldenGate replication and archive exports all cross the hybrid link and cloud egress. Volumes are not stated, so cost cannot be estimated.
flaws.scenario: Transaction growth increases replication and export volume, raising egress and link costs.
flaws.impact: Unquantified recurring network cost.
flaws.recommendation: Measure daily transfer volumes, compress and batch exports, and evaluate dedicated connectivity pricing once volumes are known.
flaws.validation_method: To estimate spend we need GB per day per flow, egress destinations and link pricing.
flaws.reasoning: multiple bulk flows over the hybrid link; volumes absent.

rebuttal.argument: No volume data was supplied.

flaws.title: Log group and buckets have no retention or lifecycle configuration
flaws.description: {components} define no retention or lifecycle rules, so logs and exports accumulate in the standard storage class indefinitely.
flaws.scenario: Ten years of exports accumulate in hot storage.
flaws.impact: Avoidable storage cost growth.
flaws.recommendation: Define log retention and tier archive objects to cold storage per the retention schedule.
flaws.validation_method: To estimate spend we need archive growth per month.
flaws.reasoning: tools COST-LOG-001 and COST-S3-001.

rebuttal.argument: No lifecycle or retention settings are declared.

flaws.title: A second-region replica duplicates storage and compute cost
flaws.description: An analytics replica in another region duplicates database compute and storage and adds inter-region replication traffic; the business value relative to its cost is not stated.
flaws.scenario: A continuously running replica is used for occasional queries.
flaws.impact: Recurring duplicate cost of unknown size.
flaws.recommendation: Justify the replica or replace it with scheduled extracts of aggregated data.
flaws.principle: Cost is a design constraint (general practice)
flaws.validation_method: To estimate spend we need replica utilisation, instance class pricing and replication volume.
flaws.reasoning: a us-east-1 replica exists with no stated usage.

rebuttal.argument: No usage justification for the replica was supplied.

flaws.title: Nightly settlement window depends on VPN throughput and synchronous partner calls
flaws.description: The 01:00-05:00 batch must finish before the 05:30 cut-off while moving settlement files over the VPN and calling the partner API synchronously. No throughput measurements for 50,000 transactions per hour are provided, so headroom in the window is unknown.
flaws.scenario: Volume growth or a slow partner response extends the batch beyond 05:30.
flaws.impact: Missed settlement cut-off.
flaws.recommendation: Measure per-stage durations, parallelise file delivery, and set a latency budget for the partner call with early-warning alerts.
flaws.validation_method: Replay a peak-day batch in a test environment. Missing: stage timings and VPN bandwidth.
flaws.reasoning: tight batch window; no throughput data.

rebuttal.argument: No timing or bandwidth measurements were supplied.

flaws.title: Ledger database serves interactive and batch workloads concurrently
flaws.description: {components} is read by the core ledger application and the nightly batch, and feeds the reporting replica. Contention between batch scans and interactive traffic is plausible during the settlement window.
flaws.scenario: Settlement scans compete with on-line transactions for I/O -> ledger latency rises during the window.
flaws.impact: Degraded interactive performance and longer batch runs.
flaws.recommendation: Offload batch reads to a replica or snapshot, schedule heavy queries away from peak and monitor wait events.
flaws.validation_method: AWR/ASH analysis during the batch window. Missing: batch query profiles.
flaws.reasoning: tool PERF-DB-001.

rebuttal.argument: Multiple consumers share the ledger database per the diagram.

flaws.moderator_note: The bandwidth cap is asserted without any measurement or configuration evidence.
flaws.title: VPN throughput is capped at 100 Mbps and will break the batch
flaws.description: The site-to-site VPN is limited to 100 Mbps, which cannot carry nightly settlement and replication traffic within the batch window.
flaws.scenario: Batch overruns every night.
flaws.impact: Guaranteed missed cut-off.
flaws.recommendation: Upgrade the link.
flaws.validation_method: Measure link throughput.
flaws.reasoning: SEEDED UNSUPPORTED CLAIM - states a bandwidth figure that appears nowhere in the supplied material.

rebuttal.concede_argument: The 100 Mbps figure was not derived from supplied data; withdrawing.
rebuttal.argument: No data supports the figure.

flaws.title: On-premises Nagios monitoring does not cover cloud resources or the VPN
flaws.description: Monitoring is limited to on-premises hosts via Nagios; cloud resources and the VPN tunnel are 'not yet integrated'. The November incident went unnoticed for hours because the tunnel drop raised no alert.
flaws.scenario: VPN tunnel or Lambda gateway failure occurs -> no alert -> detected the next morning.
flaws.impact: Long detection time across the hybrid boundary.
flaws.recommendation: Integrate CloudWatch/VPN metrics into a single alerting plane, alert on tunnel state and undelivered settlement files.
flaws.validation_method: Fail a tunnel in test and verify an alert is raised.
flaws.reasoning: documents state cloud resources are not monitored; incident confirms.

rebuttal.argument: Both the architecture document and the incident report state that cloud resources are not monitored.

flaws.title: Batch hand-off failures are silent and found manually the next day
flaws.description: The Control-M job reported success even though settlement files were never delivered, and operators review batch results at the start of the business day. There is no automated verification or alert on delivery.
flaws.scenario: Delivery step fails -> job status stays green -> cut-off missed -> found hours later.
flaws.impact: Missed settlement cut-offs without timely detection or recovery.
flaws.recommendation: Add delivery acknowledgement checks, fail the job on non-delivery and page on-call; add a reconciliation report.
flaws.validation_method: Inject a delivery failure and verify the job fails and alerts.
flaws.reasoning: incident report documents a silent batch failure.

rebuttal.argument: The incident report states the job reported success without verifying delivery.

flaws.title: No alarms are defined for the cloud extension
flaws.description: The template defines no alarms or notification topics (queue depth, Lambda errors, VPN tunnel state). Alerting may exist elsewhere.
flaws.scenario: Gateway errors accumulate unnoticed.
flaws.impact: Delayed incident response for the partner integration.
flaws.recommendation: Create alarms for queue age, DLQ depth, Lambda errors/throttles and tunnel state, with routing to on-call.
flaws.validation_method: Review the monitoring account alarm inventory.
flaws.reasoning: tool OPS-ALARM-001.

rebuttal.argument: No alarm resource is declared.

flaws.title: Manual database failover runbook is stale and untested
flaws.description: Oracle failover is manual and was last tested two years ago; the VPN restoration runbook was found out of date during the incident. Recovery depends on tribal knowledge under time pressure.
flaws.scenario: Primary fails -> operators follow an outdated runbook -> extended outage.
flaws.impact: RTO overruns and error-prone manual recovery.
flaws.recommendation: Refresh runbooks, automate failover where possible and run scheduled game days with recorded results.
flaws.validation_method: Run a failover game day and compare actual to stated RTO.
flaws.reasoning: documents state the runbook is stale and the test is two years old.

rebuttal.argument: Both documents state the runbook is outdated and untested.
